az_reef_rock_on_mica_mt.blurb: Reef Rock is a big granite wall on Mica Mountain in the Rincon Mountains southeast of Tucson, inside the Saguaro Wilderness. The cliff stands about 600 feet tall and the base sits near 7,200 feet. Climbing is almost all traditional, with eight lines running from the 5.7 range up to a single hard route near 5.12. The headline line is a four-pitch crack and chimney system of roughly 750 feet, and there is also a short, steep crack. This is a remote backcountry objective, so plan a full day, bring two ropes for the way down, and expect a rack with some big pieces.

az_wailing_wall.blurb: Wailing Wall is a small cliff in the Bear Canyon stretch of the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson. Its eight routes split evenly between sport and trad, from about 5.7 to 5.11, with the largest cluster around 5.10. The face points south, so it is a warm wall, which makes a nice contrast with the shady, pine-covered feel of much of Bear Canyon. The walk in is short but involves scrambling down sloping ledges, where cairns help mark the way.

az_casa_grande.blurb: Casa Grande is a small cluster of granite formations inside North Mountain Park, at the edge of the city of Casa Grande in central Arizona's low desert. Eight routes cover sport, top-rope and one trad line, rated from about 5.4 to 5.10, so both beginners and intermediate climbers have something to try. The rock is rough granite, and you can drive right up to the formations, which gives the place a casual, short-outing feel. Look carefully before reaching into cracks, since bees and desert wildlife use them. Summers here are very hot, so cooler months are the sensible choice.

az_continuum_crag.blurb: Continuum Crag is a sport crag at roughly 7,500 feet on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson. It is one of the two main walls of the Spectrum Crags group, above upper Sabino Canyon. The eight bolted routes start around 5.8 and climb to the 5.12 range, with most falling in the 5.10 and 5.11 bands. The stone is high quality, and the north-side lines are better than they look from below. The faces turn in several directions, so you can pick sun or shade by wall. Spectrum Wall is a short step away, making a two-wall day easy. The route in is long and tricky to follow, so go with someone who knows it.

az_west_fork.blurb: West Fork is a side canyon of Oak Creek Canyon in northern Arizona, at about 6,000 feet. Tall sandstone walls rise above springs and a small stream, and the trad lines here are long, several running six to nine pitches. The eight routes are demanding: one near 5.9, one at 5.10, and the rest bunched between 5.11 and 5.12. Climbs in the deeper reaches of the canyon are steep and committing, so this suits experienced parties more than newcomers. The canyon is also busy with hikers and canyoneers, so expect company on the approach.
